summary: Jayashree D. Sathe is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She has worked at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as editor-in-chief (attested 2011) and as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner works in archaeology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge (BA, PhD), Harvard, London, and the Courtauld Institute (MA). His posts include the Courtauld Institute (1991–1999) and Oxford, as professor of Late Antique art from 2014.

Jean Boisselier was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Philippe Stern and Pierre Dupont, attending the École du Louvre and the Sorbonne. He served at the National Museum of Cambodia and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1963–1980).
Jean Buhot was a specialist in archaeology, Japanology, and sinology. He served as Professor of Chinese and Japanese Art at the École du Louvre in 1936 and as Professor of Japanese at INALCO in 1940.

Jean Carl was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. His career included posts at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1928–1932) and the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (~1936–1940).

Jean Dantinne is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Liège and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He served as a lecturer at the University of Liège (1975) and became a professor at UCLouvain in 1983.

Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966) and served as a researcher and associate member at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, as well as an associate member at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1966–2019).

Jean Deny was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. Educated at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and Paris Faculty of Law, he taught at ENLOV (~1908–1948), the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1938–1948), and Georgetown University (1949–1953).

Jean Ferdinand Caius was an Indologist and scientist educated at the University of Paris, St. Mary's College, and St Beuno's. He served as a pharmacologist at the Haffkine Institute (1924–1932) and taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1932).

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Renou. He directed the French Institute of Pondicherry and the EFEO (1956–1977), and held chairs at the EPHE (1941–1978) and Collège de France (1951–1978).

Jean Haudry was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and under Armand Minard. He held long-term academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1967–2002) and Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (~1974–2002).

Jean Herbert was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Sri Aurobindo in 1934. He served at the League of Nations (~1919–1939), the United Nations (1945–1954), and taught Eastern mythologies at the University of Geneva (1954–1964).

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indo-European linguistics and Indology. Educated at the University of Liège and under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg, he held posts at Mainz, Liège, and joined the Collège de France in 1993.

Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist. An alumnus of the École polytechnique (~1964–1966), he served at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1986) and directed the École Polytechnique (~1992–2005).

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Kern and Uhlenbeck at the University of Amsterdam. He served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and later as a director at Leiden University (1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at EFEO, INALCO (1913–1933), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Varenne was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the EPHE and under Jean Haudry. He held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1962–1980) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (1981–1987).

Jean-Antoine Dubois was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris. He directed the Seminary of Pondicherry (1813–1819) and later served as supérieur of the Paris Foreign Missions Society (1836).

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a physicist, astronomer, and historian who studied under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace at the École Polytechnique. He served as professor of physics at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and taught at the University of Paris.

Jean-Denis Lanjuinais was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed a doctorate of laws at the University of Rennes, where he became Professor of Canonic Law in 1775, later joining the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1808.
